proposals.claim: Garment labeled as 100% silk without third-party fiber analysis documentation
proposals.rationale: Claims about fiber composition lack verifiable evidence and expose quality assurance gaps. Unsubstantiated material claims mislead consumers and undermine trust in product specifications.
constraints: Requires independent lab testing (ISO 1833 methods)
Must distinguish between claimed and actual fiber content
Cannot rely solely on supplier documentation without verification
Testing must be conducted by accredited textile laboratory
evidenceNeeded: Third-party fiber analysis report from ISO 17050 accredited lab
Chain of custody documentation for tested samples
Comparison between claimed composition and test results
Photomicrograph evidence of fiber identification

proposals.claim: Stripe repeat pattern specified at 25mm ±0.5mm without pattern continuity verification
proposals.rationale: Precise stripe measurements on sewn garments require validation across seams and across full pattern. Tolerance specification without measurement methodology or acceptance criteria creates ambiguity in production quality control.
constraints: Must specify measurement location (seam to seam vs pattern to pattern)
Requires documentation of how repeat is measured on curved surfaces
Cannot specify tolerance tighter than manufacturing capability
Must account for fabric shrinkage post-dyeing
evidenceNeeded: Calibrated measurement documentation across minimum 5 pattern repeats
Photographic evidence with scale reference showing stripe continuity at seams
Fabric shrinkage test results (ISO 5077)
Production specification sheet with clearly defined tolerance acceptance zones

proposals.claim: Garment color matches approved Pantone reference without spectrophotometer documentation or lighting condition specification
proposals.rationale: Color perception varies significantly with lighting, observer angle, and reference fatigue. Without controlled measurement conditions and instrumental validation, color matching claims remain subjective and unverifiable.
constraints: Requires spectrophotometer readings at standardized illuminants (D65, A, or specified)
Must specify deltaE acceptable variance (CIE76, CIE94, or CIEDE2000)
Visual assessment alone insufficient without instrument backing
Cannot claim match without documented reference swatch age and storage conditions
evidenceNeeded: Spectrophotometric measurement data (L*, a*, b* values) with illuminant specification
DeltaE calculation with stated acceptable threshold
Digital color reference photograph under standardized lighting (5000K minimum)
Documented reference swatch with manufacture date and storage conditions

proposals.claim: Trousers provide optimal seat drape and fit without specification of body type, fabric weight, or measurement point validation
proposals.rationale: Garment drape is subjective and dependent on wearer morphology, movement, and fabric properties. Claims of optimal fit require quantified measurements, defined body parameters, and acceptance criteria linked to specific wear conditions.
constraints: Cannot claim drape quality without specifying intended body type ranges
Requires fabric weight/hand measurements (oz/yd² or g/m²)
Seat/ease measurement must be referenced to specific size grading
Must distinguish between as-sewn and worn appearance
evidenceNeeded: Fabric weight specification with tolerance (ISO 3801)
Detailed grading specifications showing ease at seat across size range
Flat pattern measurements at seat level with defined reference points
Fit test documentation on specified demographic (age range, height/weight ranges)

proposals.claim: Shirt collar functions equally well when worn untucked or with necktie without design conflict analysis
proposals.rationale: Collar construction, stand height, and point angle create geometric constraints. Wearing modes have conflicting requirements (tie knot coverage vs untucked visibility). Claims must address design resolution or acknowledge limitation.
constraints: Collar stand height must be specified (mm) relative to neckline seam
Point length and angle cannot simultaneously optimize both wear modes
Necktie knot width creates minimum required collar throat depth
Must document whether design favors one wear mode
evidenceNeeded: Detailed collar pattern specifications including stand height and point angles
Neckline seam location measurement relative to collar stand
Visual documentation of collar appearance in both untucked and with-tie configurations
Design trade-off analysis explaining compromises or resolution method

proposals.claim: Short sleeve shirt features French cuff construction without acknowledgment of functional conflict
proposals.rationale: French cuffs require wrist-length sleeves and cufflinks for closure. Short sleeves cannot accommodate this construction. Simultaneous claim of both features represents design impossibility or unclear specification.
constraints: Cannot claim French cuff on sleeves shorter than wrist length
Must specify exact sleeve length measurement (center back neck to cuff edge)
Must clarify whether cuff is decorative or functional
Cufflink accommodation requires minimum sleeve opening diameter
evidenceNeeded: Sleeve length specification in inches/centimeters with measurement point definition
Pattern detail showing cuff construction method (fold-back, attached, sewn-through)
Cufflink hole/button specification or acknowledgment of decorative-only function
Photographic documentation of actual sleeve on specified size (with measurements visible)

proposals.claim: Trousers deliver proper cropped length with full break without defining break type or rise measurement
proposals.rationale: Cropped and full break represent contradictory length specifications. Cropped implies shortened/minimal fabric break at shoe; full break means fabric covers shoe opening with fold. Claims must resolve contradiction with measured specifications.
constraints: Cannot specify both cropped and full break simultaneously without clarification
Break specification requires inseam measurement from rise point to hem
Must account for shoe heel height variation (1-2 inches difference common)
Cropped length typically 1-2 inches shorter than full break
evidenceNeeded: Inseam measurement specification (center crotch seam to hem edge) in inches/centimeters
Visual reference photos showing trouser break on multiple shoe heel heights
Definition of break type used (no break, slight break, full break, cropped)
Size-specific length documentation with grading increment between sizes

proposals.claim: Garment quality accepted by owner and tailor without pre-defined acceptance criteria or dispute resolution mechanism
proposals.rationale: Subjective acceptance by different parties creates undefined standards and unresolvable disputes. Quality claims require documented criteria, measurement points, and pre-agreed acceptance thresholds before delivery or wear.
constraints: Acceptance criteria must be documented before garment completion
Cannot rely on single party assessment for multi-party use cases
Requires written acknowledgment of specific measured points
Must specify who makes final determination and dispute resolution path
evidenceNeeded: Written quality specification signed before production begins
Documented acceptance checklist with specific measurements (seam straightness, hem level, button placement) in mm
Pre-agreed photograph standards for visual acceptance (lighting, angles, wear duration)
Owner and tailor sign-off documentation on delivery, with specific accepted/rejected elements listed
